data.description:
Turn-based tactics in the browser. One fight, then the map shrinks. No install. No wallet to start
🟦
data.name: Heroes Of Crypto (HOCAI)

data.text:
Fire Elements and 100% magic-resistance units take nothing and block it. Passes a Water Shield without breaking it; still fires if the main blow is dodged. Attack bonuses raise it too. Pack the file and risk the splash, or leave a gap behind every stack?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

Black Dragon Fire Breath: each melee attack or answer also burns whoever stands directly behind the target on the strike line, friend or foe, for 100% of its melee damage against them at full stack. Armor applies; magic resistance cuts it. One cell behind a 1×1, two behind a 2×2.

Stack power scales it: +5% per point, so that 25% is only at full stack. Diagonals count. Do you flank wide for the bonus, or pin the Scavenger so it never gets behind?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

Scavenger Backstab: when it stands beyond its target along the line of advance — nearer the target army's starting edge, diagonals count — melee attacks and answers deal +25% at full stack, plus 1% per luck. Second strikes don't get it.

The target still answers the frightening blow itself. Spells aren't blocked. A frightened Hydra's Lightning Spin skips that Manticore too. Mind resistance cuts the roll. Peel the Manticore first, or eat the gaze and trade elsewhere?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

A Manticore's Terrifying Gaze: each of its own landed melee attacks (not answers) has 60% at full stack, plus luck, to frighten the target for one lap. It can't attack, shoot at, or answer that Manticore, but may hit anyone else. Madness and Mechanism never take it.

Stacks with 100% magic resistance skip the roar, and a stack already roaring can't take another. Quagmire and Hamstrung still cut those extra steps. Do you roar before the charge, or hold it for the mid-fight push?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

Behemoth's Battle Roar is once per fight, and only from stack power 3 up. For two laps the whole army — the Behemoth too — gets +1 movement per living Behemoth in that stack and always rolls max damage, even under Curse.

Flesh Shield does not soften it: the gaze is priced from the full hit before the aura takes its share. Do you open Medusa on the swarm or the lone finisher?
https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

A Medusa hit does two things past the damage. Part of it becomes whole creatures killed. Then a petrify roll can take the front one: 15% on a level-1 target at full stack, 27% on a level-4. Madness and Mechanism shrug both.

Buffs and heals on its allies stay free. The lock ends early if that Pikeman dies, and it does not reapply while active. Mind resistance cuts the roll. Open on a shooter or a melee threat first?

https://t.co/EENa0HvsTL

A Pikeman's Aggr: every landed melee hit or answer has 50% at full stack, plus luck, to lock the target for one lap. It may attack, shoot, or cast at enemies only at that Pikeman. Madness and Mechanism never take it.

A Manticore's Terrifying Gaze can frighten it out of the spin. Pack around it or peel off?
https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS
Lightning Spin: every Hydra attack and retaliation hits every enemy touching it, each with its own dodge roll. While the Hydra isn't Broken, those hits can't be answered.

At full stack the cut is 40 percent, and it hits Mechanism harder. Might's Abilities power synergy can push the cut further. Do you open on the shooter that has to reposition, or the melee stack that still answers from that cell?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

A Mantis that lands a melee hit can pin the target for one lap: it cannot move, and its weapon hits are cut. Spells and Fire Breath keep full damage. Pin the stack that needs a new cell, not the one that can still cast from here.

Large units need a clear 2x2 before the board eats the edge. Seat them early, or the square you wanted is already gone.

Where do you put Black Dragon or Angel on lap one?
https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS
Black Dragon and Angel are large flying finishers, but both need room for a 2x2 body. On a board that deletes outer cells, that open square is the plan.

One in the Field is the exception to the once-per-lap rule. It still never answers a shot, and Stun, Blindness, Freeze, Shadow Touch or Terrifying Gaze can still stop an answer.

Would you open into a Unicorn, or peel it first?

Play: https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

Most stacks answer once a lap. A Unicorn answers every melee hit.

Pile Double Punch into it and you take both answers — unless its first Blindness cancels your second strike.

Aura Range adds 1, 2 or 3 cells to every aura, this one included. Do you dive the Griffin or peel the shooters first?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

Enemy shooters within 2 cells of a Griffin can neither shoot nor return fire. Range Null Field is why you put a flyer on their line on purpose, not as a flourish.

Might's Aura Range synergy makes that bubble bigger.

Centaur 73, Beholder 22, Monk 8, Champion 3, Angel 2. Split an unsplit stack in half and both halves usually drop from stack power 5 to 3. Which stack do you open with?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS
A Peasant stack arrives as 200 bodies. A Black Dragon arrives as one. Both are worth about 1,000 experience. Judge the whole stack and its job, not the one figure you can see.

Dryad experience is 11. Wandering Mage is 6.466 so 1,000 experience buys 155. Scavenger stays at 6.1. Which stack do you still draft first after the retune?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

We kept the same Arachna line and the same Cyclops, then moved the numbers. Spider is attack 31 for 55–70. The Queen keeps 32 / 54–78 with armor 40 and 200 health. Cyclops is 22 attack, 18–23, 72 health, armor 19. Same picks, different weights.

One catch: you can't open it while either of you is in a live ranked or lobby game.

What would you test first with a friend: a full shooter line or one huge melee stack?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

Want to test a strange build against a friend without risking your rating? Open a co-op sandbox and invite one friend: you take green, they take red, same board. Sandbox fights never touch the ladder. Break the build there, then take it into ranked.

Hovering a unit shows its real chance: luck 7 reads 37%. The slow doesn't stack or refresh, and partial resistance won't lower the chance.

Would you put it on shooters or on melee that trades hits?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

Rime Charm, from v0.1.7: every hit your army lands, retaliations and splash included, has a 30% chance plus luck to put Quagmire on the target, -25% movement for 3 laps.

Add a Dryad's Hamstrung and a flyer keeps about half its movement. A Black Dragon is never slowed.

Same math with a 50% Magic Shield on top: that 15% unit ends up near 65%. It cuts magic damage and the chance a debuff spell lands.

Would you spend an artifact pick on it against a caster army?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

Aegis of the Arcane gives every unit in your army its own 18% magic-defense roll.

It doesn't add, it stacks: a unit with 15% ends up near 30%, not 33%, because each roll only blocks what the last one let through.

It won't stop Stun, Freeze, Paralysis, Blindness or the gazes.

Wind Flow counts too, but only its armor: with the Tome in the Valkyrie's army your flyers get +5.4 armor, enemy flyers still get +4, and every flyer still loses 4 movement.

Which caster would you build the Tome around?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

Tome of Amplification: every buff your units cast on your own army works at 135%.

Magic Mirror 40% becomes 54%. Fireforged Sword 20% becomes 27%. A Behemoth's Battle Roar gives +1.35 movement per Behemoth, not +1.

Heal and Resurrection don't count.

Worth the pick in PvP?

The other way to hold is Luck Shield: luck set to +3 for the lap (capped at +10), 2 morale, and the turn ends. While any stack with Time Denial is alive, nobody can wait.

What's worth giving up your place in the queue for?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

Waiting isn't free. Hourglass sends your stack to the very end of the lap, after even the Dismorale stacks, and costs 3 morale. It works once per lap, and your last stack still to act can't wait at all.

Wait only when you know which better turn you're buying.

ttps://heroesofcrypto.io/playhThich one would you pick for a shooter army?
Whe shooter's luck adds to the chance: at luck +7 the artifact card reads 47%. It can't be taken with Rime Charm or Gravechain, since each army gets one Tier 2 artifact.

Quiver of Echoes gives every ranged attack a 40% chance to fire one more full-strength volley, splash and piercing included. Double Shot and Double Throw still work, so a Gargantuan can throw three times. The echo uses normal ammo, can't echo again and grants no extra counter.

No rise while Broken, or after a death to poison, the shrinking board or a later Armageddon wave. Casting Resurrection on another stack spends the self-rise too.

Do you hit the Angels first, or leave them for last?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

We got one wrong. When an Angel stack is wiped out, half the fallen Angels rise again at full health, once per fight. The rules brought them back, but the board could leave them frozen in their death pose. Since v0.1.7 the risen Angels drop the corpse frame and stand up.

Miss your first deadline of a ranked fight and the game plays Hourglass (or Luck Shield) for that stack. Both cost morale.

Do you spend the budget early on your big stacks, or save it for the end of the lap?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

Every ranked PvP turn runs on a clock. Your army gets a 4-minute budget for the lap, and one turn can take up to 60 seconds of it, but the game always keeps at least 12 seconds for each stack that still has to act. Once per lap you can ask for extra time.

Morale rolls cut in first, Dismorale and Hourglass waiters go last. In lap one the army with higher average morale starts.

A drafted unit can be split into stacks during placement. Would you split to win the tail of the lap?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

Turn order in Heroes of Crypto isn't one speed list.

Armies alternate one stack at a time, each sending its highest-initiative stack that hasn't acted. When one army runs out, the other's stacks go back to back.

So out-stack your opponent and you get moves in a row.

Retaliation hits count too, and positive luck raises the 50%. It's a Tier 2 pick, so it can't go with Quiver of Echoes or Rime Charm.

Would you slow your own army for it?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

Gravechain is a cursed artifact. Every unit in your own army loses 1 movement step, flyers and shooters included. In return, every hit you land rolls 50% per enemy, along up to 3 links of touching cells, to bind them: 25% less movement for 3 laps.

The map is fixed when the draft is created. Spymaster sees it with the starting bundle; Scout and Battle Trance get it after the Level-2 picks, before Level 3. Battle Trance also gets no ban summary.

Which would you pick?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

Before a ranked PvP draft you choose how much of the other army you get to see. Spymaster watches every creature pick and knows the map from the start, for 5 augment points. Scout watches three slots, for 6. Battle Trance drafts blind, for 7. Less scouting buys a stronger army.

It can't target the Satyr itself or another Satyr stack. With Tome of Amplification the ally gets more, while the Satyr still gives up 30%.

Would you hit the weakened Satyr or the buffed ally first?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

Our Satyr can lend its own body. Helping Hand gives an ally's creatures 30% of one Satyr's max health and base armor for 3 laps, and the Satyr loses the same.

Since v0.1.7 a golden link on the board joins the two stacks. If either stack dies, the bonus and the penalty both end.

Morale rolls at lap start: at +20, a 20% chance to act ahead of the queue with 1.25x damage. A kill gives +4 to the stack that made it; a lost stack costs 4 to your other stacks of that unit. Waiting costs 3, Defend 2.

Chase their centre or hold?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

There's almost no neutral step in our PvP fights. A move that ends closer to the centre of the enemy army gives that stack +3 morale; one that ends farther away costs 3. Even a sideways step counts one way or the other. Only ending at exactly the same distance is neutral.

Dead bodies count toward a stack's health for the waves, so the first three add up to 150% and wave 3 finishes almost everything. A Water Shield absorbs one wave, but only ever wave 1.

Do you play for the early kill or try to outlast them?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

Every PvP fight has a clock. From lap 12, each lap opens with an Armageddon wave on both armies: 25%, then 50%, 75% and 100% of each stack's starting health. Armor and luck don't reduce it. A fight that reaches lap 15 ends in a draw, so waiting it out wins nothing.

The trade-off: its morale is always 0 and Mind spells and poison can't touch it, but Stun and Freeze land 1.5x as often and physical area and line attacks hit it 50% harder.

Do you wall it in, or spend it early?

https://t.co/gdYw9HVfcS

Design call: our guide once said Resurrection worked on the Tsar Cannon. We decided it shouldn't. A Mechanism unit can't be healed or brought back, and an Angel's Resurrection never lands on one. Lose the cannon and it stays lost, so you guard it or trade it on purpose.
